It's cheap: about 12 times trailing earnings and a quarter of annual sales, for a niche western-and-workwear chain with real pricing power. The catch is honest — sales grew 10.7% only because they opened stores and had an extra week; same-store sales were flat, profit per dollar of sales fell from 3.3% to 2.3%, and they carry $462m of debt against $32m of cash. Second checkpoint: the full-year print roughly 12 months out, judged against management's own flat-SSS guide.
results.rerating_horizon: 2-4 years, honest and wide. This is a comps-and-margin repair plus new-store-growth story, not a catalyst trade — it only re-rates after 2-4 consecutive quarters of positive same-store sales alongside year-over-year gross-margin expansion. If comps stay flat, the shares plausibly sit near today's ~0.59x enterprise-value-to-sales for the whole period and the position simply does nothing. The width of that band is itself the reason size is 0.5% rather than the sleeve's 1-2%.

Left QUALITATIVE deliberately: the two-consecutive-quarter persistence requirement cannot be captured by a single metric reading, so no point-trigger is armed.
